popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: In the Gigantomachy Athena flays the Giant Pallas and uses his skin as a shield — the named etiology for one strand of the aegis tradition.

popCulture.title: Pallas (Giant)
popCulture.description: Earthborn Giant whom Athena kills and flays — carefully distinct from the Titan Pallas, father of Nike, and from Athena's own epithet Pallas.

popCulture.title: Aegis
popCulture.description: One ancient account makes the aegis the flayed hide of the Giant Pallas — rival etiologies name the Gorgon or Asterus instead.

popCulture.title: Gigantomachy
popCulture.description: The battle of Olympians and Giants in which Athena's flaying of Pallas stands beside Enceladus under Sicily and Polybotes under Nisyros.

popCulture.title: Pallas Athena
popCulture.description: A fragment of Epicharmus links Athena's byname Pallas to her victory over the Giant — one of several contested origins for the epithet.
